title: Indo-Afro Sunrise
project: Indo-Afro Sunrise — single piece, delivered stereo and 7.1
medium: album / playlist single that also has to work as an installation loop
brief: happy upbeat indo afro, in an immersive ambience of nature, 8-channel
audience: a listener on headphones first, then a room with an 8-channel ring; nobody is watching a picture
purpose: lift the room for a minute and put the listener inside a canopy at first light, with the groove coming from the ground and the birds above it
point_of_view: the listener standing in a forest clearing as the sun comes through: close to the players, inside the trees
job: make the body move before the first chorus (the groove is the reason the piece exists)
carry an Indian voice (tanpura, bansuri, tabla, sitar) inside an Afrobeat rhythm section without either becoming a decoration
place the listener in the canopy: the ambience is a space, not a pad, and it survives the fold to stereo
end on the tonic with the drone still sounding, so the loop can restart
story: A drone fades in with the shaker, a bamboo flute calls twice, and by bar 9 the kit, bass and highlife guitar have taken over; the chorus lifts the flute an octave while the sitar crosses behind the listener, and after the last brass stab the groove thins to the drone and the canopy.

sections.name: dawn
sections.action: light comes through the canopy; the clearing is empty
sections.music: tanpura drone, shekere from bar 1, djembe from bar 5, two bansuri calls, the highlife guitar from bar 3

sections.name: grove
sections.action: the players arrive and the ground starts to move
sections.music: kit, bass, marimba arpeggio and tabla enter; the flute states the theme in full

sections.name: high_sun
sections.action: full sun: the clearing is loud with insects and the groove is at its widest
sections.music: brass stabs, sitar 16ths crossing behind, the flute an octave up, crash on the downbeat

sections.name: golden_hour
sections.action: the light thins; the canopy is heard again
sections.music: brass out, flute back down an octave, sitar returns at bar 29, the drone is left alone from bar 30

motifs.name: the call
motifs.shape: A4 up a step to B4, then a fourth up to E5 held
motifs.returns: in the grove at bar 9 in the same register, an octave up in the chorus from bar 17, and alone on A4 at bar 30

motifs.name: the skank
motifs.shape: three-note highlife chord on the off-beats, never on beat one
motifs.returns: every bar from 3 to 32, thinning to two hits in golden_hour

avoid_sounds: field recordings of rain that are not in the canopy preset

hits.sound: crash, brass stab and the flute jumping an octave on the downbeat of bar 17
hits.why: the chorus has to arrive as a place, not as a louder verse

hits.sound: brass stops, the sitar enters and the canopy comes up 2 dB
hits.why: the turn into golden_hour is a change of air, so it is a subtraction, not a hit

must_hear: the tanpura alone in the first two bars
the shekere before the kit enters at 17.1 s
the brass stab on the downbeat at 34.3 s
the sitar crossing from the right to behind at 42 s
mix_intent.executed_by: carried on the score as mix_intent; the mix preset reads it with lead_carve {enabled, from_intent}

delivery.played_on: headphones and a phone (stereo), and an 8-channel ring of loudspeakers (7.1, FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR)

references: bansuri phrasing in a bright raga

immersive.why: the brief asks for an immersive ambience of nature: the canopy has to be above and around the listener, the sitar has to pass behind, and the eight channels are the delivery, so a stereo-only mix would lose the thing that was asked for

movers.why: the Indian answer crosses the listener instead of sitting in one speaker
movers.path: starts 75 degrees right at 3 m, passes 95 degrees right by bar 21 and ends 110 degrees right at 3.2 m by bar 24

movers.why: the arpeggio drifts left into the trees so the groove has depth
movers.path: starts 45 degrees left at 3.5 m, drifts to 80 degrees left by bar 16 and to 100 degrees by bar 24

movers.why: the flute is the figure, so it only breathes across the front: a small move keeps it the hero
movers.path: 8 degrees right at 2.4 m, 10 degrees left at 2 m by bar 17, back to 14 degrees right by bar 24

room_changes.why: the canopy thins: the room gets longer and darker as the sun drops

must_hear: the canopy above and behind at the start
the sitar crossing from the right to behind at 42 s
the shekere on the right edge
the drone at 0 degrees when everything else has stopped
immersive.notes: the sheet records the intent; the mix preset carries the height table and the engine, the space preset carries the room, and the score carries the keyframes. 7.1 is rendered, not folded, and its own channel order is FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR.

expression.sonic_picture: First ten seconds: a tanpura drone with a shekere and a single bamboo flute call, the canopy audible above and behind. By the middle the kit, bass and highlife guitar are running and the flute is an octave up with the sitar crossing behind. The last note is A4 held over the drone, with the canopy fading after it.
expression.performer: A bansuri player breathes in the gaps and leans into the long E5, with a slide up into it; the djembe and tabla players answer each other on the off-beats and never play the same stroke; the guitarist plays the skank short and lets it ring only on the last bar of each phrase.
expression.producer_moves: The canopy comes up 2 dB into golden_hour, the reverb send on the flute grows with the section energy, the sitar is panned by trajectory rather than by a static pan, and the last bar has no kit at all.
expression.anti_generic: The generic version of this brief is a four-on-the-floor kick with a 'world' flute sample and a rain loop; what stops it here is a kick on 1, 2&, 3 and 4 with the snare displaced, a tabla and a djembe that trade strokes, a tanpura that is the harmonic floor rather than a pad, and a melody that is one shape varied four ways instead of a scale run.

theme.contour: arch: a step up, a fourth up to a held note, then a stepwise fall
theme.interval_character: mostly steps with one fourth leap that lands on E5
theme.why_memorable: the fourth leap lands on a held note and is never transposed in the chorus, only octave-displaced
theme.variation_plan: stated in dawn, played in full in the grove, octave up in high_sun, back down and alone at bar 30

gate_reason: melodic: the piece has a figure (bansuri) carrying it over a full rhythm section, and the profile keeps every row on rather than skipping the melody rows the way groove or texture would
notes: The canopy bed is the shipped env:amazon_rainforest model (noise bed, stridulation, drips, chirp clusters) — synthesis, not a field recording. Tabla and djembe strokes are played on GM percussion keys as named stand-ins from world.py, not sampled instruments; that limit is repeated in STATUS.md. 2026-11-28: happy vocals added (a lead that calls in syllables, a group that answers; no words); stereo is the delivery. The score no longer carries placement: it lives in the presets.
